newsitem.title: CHINA: China offers rewards for reporting leprosy cases.
newsitem.headline: China offers rewards for reporting leprosy cases.

text.p: China has virtually eradicated leprosy but some local governments are offering cash rewards to people who report new cases.
The rewards go as high as 500 yuan ($60) for giving the names of people with leprosy, the Xinhua news agency said on Saturday.
China now had about 7,000 leprosy cases, and the number of newly discovered cases had fallen to 2,000 in 1995 from nearly 5,000 in 1985, Xinhua said without elaborating.
In 1957, the official estimate of the leper population in China was between 380,000 and 390,000, the agency quoted He Daxun, secretary general of the China Leprosy Association, as saying.
The World Health Organisation standard for basically wiping out leprosy is an incidence rate of 0.1 per 1,000, which China achieved in 1981, He said.
